method.sampling: median along central 50% of each edge; minimum across transverse 7 pixels
method.brightness: mean red and green; normalized by frame ROI 95th percentile yellow background
method.timing: Before/after player time brackets; neither exact decoded PTS nor native video frames
method.oldComparison: All 76 old raster reconstructions; integer translations dx -2..2, dy -1..1; no rotation/reflection; minimum edge symmetric difference. Old raster is not ground truth.

transitionFit.timingCaveat: Regression of screenshot bracket midpoints; approximate 1 Hz, not native-frame precision.

conclusions: The visible reconstruction lies on an 8 by 12 square-cell lattice in every slot.
Four slots update together at approximately one-second intervals.
One exact four-glyph state repeats at 2-3 and 11-12 seconds; this does not establish a global period.
Changing odd-degree vertex sets rule out a fixed graph modified ONLY by XOR of complete cycles, including unit squares.
Unit square cycles are present in many states, but no authoring algorithm is identified.

cycleXorHypothesis.interpretation: An XOR of complete cycles has even degree at every vertex. Odd vertices in the measured symmetric difference refute a cycle-only update for that transition; even degree is necessary and sufficient for decomposition into grid face boundaries, but does not identify the authoring algorithm.
